response.sql: SELECT p.staff_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, CAST(SUM(p.amount) AS DOUBLE) / (SELECT CAST(SUM(amount) AS DOUBLE) FROM payment WHERE rental_id IS NOT NULL) AS fraction_of_total FROM payment p WHERE p.rental_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.staff_id ORDER BY p.staff_id

assumptions.assumption: The denominator is the combined amount of only the rental-linked payments (rental_id IS NOT NULL), so the fractions sum to 1 across the returned staff rows.

Division is done in DOUBLE rather than DECIMAL. MySQL's DECIMAL division keeps only a few extra digits of scale, which would round the fraction; DOUBLE keeps full precision for the ratio. The SUM(amount) values themselves remain exact DECIMAL.

alternatives.interpretation: The denominator is the combined amount of all payments, including those with no rental_id, so the fractions show each staff member's share of total revenue while the numerator still counts only rental-linked payments.
